changed.from: Fix \(D,\Omega,H,s\) satisfying the honest BACKSHIFT model with \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\), while the compatibility set permits positive-semidefinite invariant nuisances. The equality \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) holds for every assignment of arbitrary matrices from the positive-definite replacement domain to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\) if and only if \(\delta_H>c\), equivalently \(\gamma_H>0\). changed.to: Fix an honest BACKSHIFT instance \(D,H,s,\Omega\) with \(D\in\mathcal D\), nonnegative shifts, \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\), and positive-definite honest covariances. If \(\delta_H>c\), equivalently \(\gamma_H>0\), then \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)=\{D\}\) for every assignment of matrices in \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) to the \(c\) slots in \(E\setminus H\). If, in addition, this fixed instance has \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) and \(\delta_H\le c\), then there are positive-definite values for all slots in \(E\setminus H\), a matrix \(D'\in\mathcal D\) with \(D'\ne D\), an invariant \(\Omega'\in\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\), and nonnegative shifts on a set \(H'\subseteq E\) with \(|H'|=h\) such that \(D,D'\in\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\). On the positive-definite invariant-noise interior and at \(c=0\), the equivalence is exactly the BACKSHIFT pairwise noncollinearity criterion.

changed.from:
The definition-level coverage claim is valid, but the requested computable confidence-union construction has a negative answer for the region class stated in the question.  More precisely, if
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}=\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in H\},
\]
then \(G_{n,\alpha,H}\subseteq\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\), and consequently \(\Pr(G_{n,\alpha,H})\ge 1-\alpha\) implies \(\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\ge1-\alpha\).

For a rational population covariance family \(\Sigma\), the population compatibility set \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) has an exact rational semialgebraic description.  Effective real quantifier elimination therefore supplies finite rational-polynomial certificates for infeasibility, singleton output, and multiple-candidate output.  The affine minors of the fitted diagonal shifts can be included, without division, among the sign polynomials in each certificate.  These minors certify separation, but they cannot by themselves certify feasibility: the covariance equations, positive-semidefinite invariant nuisance, nonnegative shifts, invertibility, unit diagonal, and cycle-product inequalities are also necessary.  Normalization-chart changes are sound when pivot nonvanishing and all normalization and cycle inequalities are cleared to polynomial sign conditions before a chart certificate is accepted.

In contrast, when \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) is only an arbitrary nonempty subset of \(\mathbb S_{++}^p\), as in the frozen definition, no deterministic procedure making only finitely many membership queries to these sets can return the exact full set \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) for every region family.  This failure already occurs for \(p=2\), \(m=3\), and \(c=0\), with rational positive-definite matrices and a design having affine-minor separation \(\gamma_H=1\).  Hence the complete conjunction requested in the open question is false as stated: an exact computable confidence union, and thus a computable full-output-or-abstain rule at \(\gamma_H=0\), requires an additional effective representation of the regions.  The causal target remains \(B=I_p-D\); neither the coverage inclusion nor the semialgebraic description defines that target to equal an observable functional.

Under \(\text{ass:backshift-normalization}\), \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\), and \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\), suppose additionally that \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\). For
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}=\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in H\},
\]
one has
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}\subseteq\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}.
\]
Consequently, \(\Pr(G_{n,\alpha,H})\geq1-\alpha\) implies \(\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\geq1-\alpha\).

Pointwise for every realized encoded region family, the procedure in \(\text{def:certificate-inference-handle}\) terminates. Its first quantifier-elimination output is a finite quantifier-free rational-polynomial formula whose realization is exactly the complete confidence union \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). Its audit sentence is true exactly when there exists a full feasible candidate tuple whose affine separation, cycle slack, positive-definiteness margin, condition number, or scale violates, respectively, \(\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0,\overline\kappa,\overline M\). Hence the procedure returns the exact full-union code after a clean universal audit and otherwise returns \(\mathsf{ABSTAIN}\). In particular, it abstains whenever a feasible candidate has zero affine separation.

The encoded input contract is essential for this exact symbolic conclusion in the finite-membership-query model: \(\text{lem:finite-membership-query-obstruction}\) gives rational positive-definite regions with separated affine minors for which no deterministic procedure using only finitely many membership queries computes the exact union for every arbitrary nonempty region family. No operator-norm contraction or confidence-union rate follows from this representation theorem; such a result additionally requires a proved inverse joint-diagonalization coercivity bound or a compact candidate envelope. The causal target remains \(B=I_p-D\), while \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) is an observed-region compatibility functional whose coverage relation to that target is proved above rather than imposed by definition.

Restricting the input to nonempty regions with exact finite rational-semialgebraic codes is a genuine input-class narrowing, and the supporting oracle witness shows why such effective representation is necessary. On this narrowed class, finite subset enumeration plus full feasibility formulas and effective real quantifier elimination construct the exact union and a decidable conservative margin audit.

changed.to:
For each \(n\geq1\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), let \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) be the nonempty realization of its code in \(\text{def:encoded-covariance-regions}\). Define
\[
\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}
=\bigcup_{\substack{\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\\ e\in E}}
\mathcal R_c(\Gamma).
\]
Thus \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_{\alpha}\) is the set-valued inversion of the encoded simultaneous covariance regions through the population replacement-compatibility map \(\mathcal R_c\). Coverage, computability, margin auditing, and singleton conclusions are theorem properties and are not included in this construction definition.
changed.reason: The definition currently mixes the set construction with coverage and singleton theorem claims and permits arbitrary unencoded regions. The corrected construction is the exact set-valued inversion on the encoded region class, leaving all mathematical properties to the theorem.

changed.from: Start from the finite subset enumeration in \(\text{def:subset-consensus}\), represent noncollinearity without division by homogeneous \(3\times3\) affine minors, obtain operator-norm local perturbation control from the joint-diagonalization linearization indexed by \(\gamma_H,\kappa_D,\zeta_D,\lambda_H,M_H\), invert the indexed simultaneous covariance regions, and switch normalization charts only after forming chart-valid certificates.
changed.to:
Fix a realized encoded region family, \(n\geq1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and rational thresholds \(\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0>0\) and \(\overline\kappa,\overline M\geq1\). For each \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\), introduce a candidate tuple
\[
w=(K,A,\Psi,(t_e)_{e\in K},(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K}).
\]
The full feasibility formula \(F_K(w)\) is the conjunction of: each encoded region formula at \(\Gamma_e\); \(\Gamma_e\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\); \(A_{ii}=1\); \((\det A)^2>0\); \(1-\pi_C(A)>0\) and \(1+\pi_C(A)>0\) for every directed simple cycle \(C\), where \(\pi_C(A)\) is the corresponding entry product in \(I_p-A\); \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\); \(t_{ej}\geq0\); and
\[
A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)
\qquad(e\in K).
\]
For such a tuple set \(\zeta(w)=1-\max_C|\pi_C(A)|\), \(\kappa(w)=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\),
\[
\lambda(w)=\min\left\{\lambda_{\min}(\Psi),\min_{e\in K}\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma_e)\right\},
\qquad
M(w)=1+\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\Gamma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and, writing
\[
\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)=
\det\begin{pmatrix}
1&t_{ek}&t_{e\ell}\\
1&t_{fk}&t_{f\ell}\\
1&t_{gk}&t_{g\ell}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
set \(\gamma(w)=0\) if \(h-c<3\), and otherwise set
\[
\gamma(w)=
\min_{1\leq k<\ell\leq p}
\min_{\substack{S\subseteq K\\|S|=h-c}}
\max_{e<f<g\in S}|\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)|.
\]
The certificate procedure forms
\[
\Phi_{\mathcal U}(A)
=\bigvee_{\substack{K\subseteq E\\|K|=h}}
\exists\Psi\,\exists(t_e)_{e\in K}\,\exists(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K} F_K(w),
\]
calls effective real quantifier elimination to obtain a quantifier-free rational-polynomial code in \(A\), and calls it again on the closed sentence asserting that some feasible tuple violates at least one of
\[
\gamma(w)\geq\gamma_0,\qquad
\zeta(w)\geq\zeta_0,\qquad
\lambda(w)\geq\lambda_0,\qquad
\kappa(w)\leq\overline\kappa,\qquad
M(w)\leq\overline M.
\]
It returns the code for \(\Phi_{\mathcal U}\) when that sentence is false and returns \(\mathsf{ABSTAIN}\) when it is true. This definition names the finite symbolic procedure and its candidate margins; exactness, termination, coverage, and the abstention guarantee are asserted only by the theorem.
changed.reason: The current handle promises an unproved local perturbation inversion and is not a terminating construction. The corrected handle names the finite full-feasibility projection, exact rational quantifier-elimination code, and decidable five-margin audit, without asserting confidence-union contraction.

The following certified uniform-inference result is partial and sharp with respect to the presently certified scope. If every covariance region is supplied by \(\text{def:encoded-covariance-regions}\), then, for every realized encoded region family, \(\text{CertificateInferenceHandle}\) terminates and computes a finite quantifier-free rational-polynomial code whose realization is exactly the full union \(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). It returns that code exactly when its universal five-margin audit is clean and otherwise returns \(\mathsf{ABSTAIN}\). The audit is clean exactly when every full feasible candidate has affine separation at least \(\gamma_0\), cycle slack at least \(\zeta_0\), positive-definiteness margin at least \(\lambda_0\), condition number at most \(\overline\kappa\), and scale at most \(\overline M\). For every rational population covariance family \(\Sigma\), finite rational-polynomial sentences decide whether \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) is empty, is a singleton, or has at least two elements. \[
G_{n,\alpha,H}
=\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in H\}.
\]

\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}\subseteq\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\},
\]
and hence
\[
\Pr(G_{n,\alpha,H})\geq1-\alpha
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\Pr\{D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]

\[

\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha,D)
\leq C_0r_{n,\alpha,H},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha)
\leq2C_0r_{n,\alpha,H},
\]
where
\[
L_0=(p!\,\overline\kappa^{p-1})^{1/p},\qquad
K_0=\frac{6\overline M}{\gamma_0}\sqrt{p(p-1)(1+L_0^2)},
\qquad
C_0=16K_0L_0^3.
\]
These bounds are uniform over fixed \(p,m,c,\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0,\overline\kappa,\overline M\). Along any sequence of covered outcomes on which the audit releases and \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\to0\), both displayed set radii converge to zero. For every rational population covariance family \(\Sigma\), finite rational-polynomial sentences decide whether \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) is empty, is a singleton, or has at least two elements. Fix a realized encoded region family, \(n\geq1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and rational thresholds \(\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0>0\) and \(\overline\kappa,\overline M\geq1\). For each \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\), introduce a candidate tuple
\[
w=(K,A,\Psi,(t_e)_{e\in K},(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K}).
\]
The full feasibility formula \(F_K(w)\) is the conjunction of: each encoded region formula at \(\Gamma_e\); \(\Gamma_e\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\); \(A_{ii}=1\); \((\det A)^2>0\); \(1-\pi_C(A)>0\) and \(1+\pi_C(A)>0\) for every directed simple cycle \(C\), where \(\pi_C(A)\) is the corresponding entry product in \(I_p-A\); \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\); \(t_{ej}\geq0\); and
\[
A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)
\qquad(e\in K).
\]
For such a tuple set \(\zeta(w)=1-\max_C|\pi_C(A)|\), \(\kappa(w)=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\),
\[
\lambda(w)=\min\left\{\lambda_{\min}(\Psi),\min_{e\in K}\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma_e)\right\},
\qquad
M(w)=1+\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\Gamma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and, writing
\[
\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)=
\det\begin{pmatrix}
1&t_{ek}&t_{e\ell}\\
1&t_{fk}&t_{f\ell}\\
1&t_{gk}&t_{g\ell}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
set \(\gamma(w)=0\) if \(h-c<3\), and otherwise set
\[
\gamma(w)=
\min_{1\leq k<\ell\leq p}
\min_{\substack{S\subseteq K\\|S|=h-c}}
\max_{e<f<g\in S}|\Delta^{k\ell}_{efg}(t)|.
\]
The certificate procedure forms
\[
\Phi_{\mathcal U}(A)
=\bigvee_{\substack{K\subseteq E\\|K|=h}}
\exists\Psi\,\exists(t_e)_{e\in K}\,\exists(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K} F_K(w),
\]
calls effective real quantifier elimination to obtain a quantifier-free rational-polynomial code in \(A\), and calls it again on the closed sentence asserting that some feasible tuple violates at least one of
\[
\gamma(w)\geq\gamma_0,\qquad
\zeta(w)\geq\zeta_0,\qquad
\lambda(w)\geq\lambda_0,\qquad
\kappa(w)\leq\overline\kappa,\qquad
M(w)\leq\overline M.
\]
It returns the code for \(\Phi_{\mathcal U}\) when that sentence is false and returns \(\mathsf{ABSTAIN}\) when it is true. This definition names the finite symbolic procedure and its candidate margins; exactness, termination, coverage, and the abstention guarantee are asserted only by the theorem.

Fix \(p,m,c\), put \(h=m-c\) and \(q=m-2c=h-c\), and fix rational thresholds \(\gamma _0,\zeta _0,\lambda _0>0\) and \(\overline\kappa,\overline M\geq1\).  Define
\[
 L_0=\bigl(p!\,\overline\kappa^{\,p-1}\bigr)^{1/p},\qquad
 K_0=\frac{6\overline M}{\gamma _0}
 \sqrt{p(p-1)(1+L_0^2)},
\]
\[
 \rho _0=\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{2K_0\overline M}\right\},
 \qquad C_0=16K_0L_0^3.
\]
These are effectively represented positive real algebraic numbers.

Let \(\mathfrak T\) be the finite union, over \(H_1,H_2\subseteq E\) with \(|H_1|=|H_2|=h\) and \(S\subseteq H_1\cap H_2\) with \(|S|=q\), of tuples
\[
 \tau=\bigl(H_1,H_2,S,D,U,\Omega,(s_e,\Sigma_e)_{e\in H_1},
 A,V,\Psi,(t_e,\Gamma_e)_{e\in H_2}\bigr)
\]
where \(D,U,A,V\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\), the matrices \(\Omega,\Psi,\Sigma_e,\Gamma_e\) are symmetric \(p\times p\) matrices, and \(s_e,t_e\in\mathbb R^p\), satisfying the following closed constraints.  The inverse variables obey \(DU=UD=I_p\) and \(AV=VA=I_p\).  Both \(D\) and \(A\) have unit diagonal; for every directed simple cycle \(C\), the corresponding products in \(I_p-D\) and \(I_p-A\) have absolute value at most \(1-\zeta _0\); and
\[
 \|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|U\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline\kappa,
 \qquad
 \|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|V\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline\kappa.
\]
The nuisance and covariance matrices and the shifts satisfy
\[
 \Omega,\Psi\succeq\lambda _0I_p,qquad
 \Sigma_e,\Gamma_e\succeq\lambda _0I_p,qquad
 s_e,t_e\in[0,\infty)^p,
\]
\[
 D\Sigma_eD^{\mathsf T}=\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\quad(e\in H_1),
 \qquad
 A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\quad(e\in H_2).
\]
Each of the two shift designs has affine separation at least \(\gamma _0\), with the separation computed using all subsets of its honest set having cardinality \(q\), and each side satisfies its scale bound
\[
 1+\|\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
 \max_{e\in H_1}\|\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
 \max_{e\in H_1}\|\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline M,
\]
\[
 1+\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
 \max_{e\in H_2}\|\Gamma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+
 \max_{e\in H_2}\|\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\overline M.
\]
All operator-norm, eigenvalue, and finite minimum--maximum conditions here are interpreted through their equivalent first-order real-polynomial formulas.  Define the full covariance-equation residual on the overlap by
\[
 \mathfrak r(\tau)=
 \max_{e\in S}
 \left\|A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}-\Psi-\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\right\|_{\mathrm F},
\]
and let \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) be the subfamily satisfying
\[
 \|AU-I_p\|_{\mathrm F}\geq\rho _0.
\]
Set \(\mu _0=1\) if \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}=\varnothing\), and otherwise set
\[
 \mu _0=\min_{\tau\in\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}}\mathfrak r(\tau).
\]
Starting with \(j=1,2,\ldots\), use effective real quantifier elimination to decide whether some \(\tau\in\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) has \(\mathfrak r(\tau)<2^{-j}\), and let \(\underline\mu=2^{-j}\) at the first negative answer.  Finally define
\[
 r_0=\frac{\underline\mu}{2\sqrt p\,L_0^2}.
\]
The package consisting of \(L_0,K_0,\rho _0,C_0,\mathfrak T,\mu _0,\underline\mu,r_0\) is \(\operatorname{AuditedReleaseContraction}(p,m,c,\gamma _0,\zeta _0,\lambda _0,\overline\kappa,\overline M)\).  Positivity and termination of the search are theorem properties, not part of this definition.

\[

K_0=\frac{6\overline M}{\gamma_0}\sqrt{p(p-1)(1+L_0^2)},

\[
w=(K,A,\Psi,(t_e)_{e\in K},(\Gamma_e)_{e\in K}).
\]
The full feasibility formula \(F_K(w)\) is the conjunction of: each encoded region formula at \(\Gamma_e\); \(\Gamma_e\in\mathbb S_{++}^p\); \(A_{ii}=1\); \((\det A)^2>0\); \(1-\pi_C(A)>0\) and \(1+\pi_C(A)>0\) for every directed simple cycle \(C\), where \(\pi_C(A)\) is the corresponding entry product in \(I_p-A\); \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\); \(t_{ej}\geq0\); and
\[

\qquad(e\in K).
\]
For such a tuple set \(\zeta(w)=1-\max_C|\pi_C(A)|\), \(\kappa(w)=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\),
\[
\lambda_{\mathrm{cov}}(w)=\min_{e\in K}\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma_e),
\qquad
M(w)=1+\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\Gamma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in K}\|\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and, writing
\[

\det\begin{pmatrix}
1&t_{ek}&t_{e\ell}\\
1&t_{fk}&t_{f\ell}\\
1&t_{gk}&t_{g\ell}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
set \(\gamma(w)=0\) if \(h-c<3\), and otherwise set
\[

\[

\zeta(w)\geq\zeta_0,\qquad
\lambda_{\mathrm{cov}}(w)\geq\lambda_0,\qquad
\kappa(w)\leq\overline\kappa,\qquad
M(w)\leq\overline M.

Effective real quantifier elimination is mathematically valid, but this repository has no executable certified real-closed-field QE substrate, and no smaller Lean interface can honestly retain exact code generation, termination, universal audit decidability, rational emptiness/singleton/multiplicity trichotomy, or an effectively computed contraction radius. ## Exact structured core operations

1. `def:encoded-covariance-regions` — **definition-delete**. A finite rational-semialgebraic syntax may be discussed only inside the open question/future-work text; it is no longer a delivered definition or a premise of a delivered theorem. Delete the symbol `RegionCode`.

   It has no encoding, computability, solver, audit, or decidability clause. Keep `Ualpha` as a set-valued compatibility/confidence union.

   `G_(n,alpha,H) = {Sigma_e in C^(n)_(e,alpha) for every e in H}`,
   one has `G_(n,alpha,H) subseteq {D in U^(n)_alpha}`; consequently `Pr(G_(n,alpha,H)) >= 1-alpha` implies `Pr{D in U^(n)_alpha} >= 1-alpha`. Depend only on the three structural assumptions, `def:compatible-set`, and revised `def:confidence-union` (plus `def:admissible-matrices` if the schema requires the transitive definition). The proof chooses `Gamma_e=Sigma_e` on `H`, arbitrary region members off `H`, and witnesses `(K,A,Psi,t)=(H,D,Omega,s)`. Subtracting the transformed covariance equation at environment one from those at environments two and three cancels the common invariant matrix. The differences must be diagonal, while direct multiplication gives
\[
A(\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1)A^{\mathsf T}
=\begin{pmatrix}1&y\\y&y^2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
A(\Sigma_3-\Sigma_1)A^{\mathsf T}
=\begin{pmatrix}x^2&x\\x&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Their off-diagonal entries imply \(y=0\) and \(x=0\). Thus \(A=I_2\). Conversely, \(I_2\) is compatible with invariant matrix \(2I_2\) and the displayed nonnegative shifts, so
\[
\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Sigma_3)=\{I_2\}.
\]

For each nonzero \(q\in\mathbb Q\), set
\[
A_q=\begin{pmatrix}1&q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\Psi_q=2\begin{pmatrix}1+q^2&q\\q&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\Gamma_{3,q}=\begin{pmatrix}2+q^2&-q\\-q&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The matrix \(A_q\) is invertible and has unit diagonal. The two-cycle product of \(I_2-A_q\) is zero, so \(A_q\in\mathcal D\). For every nonzero vector \(v\),
\[
v^{\mathsf T}\Psi_qv=2\|A_q^{\mathsf T}v\|_2^2>0,
\]
because \(A_q\) is invertible. If \(v=(u,w)^{\mathsf T}\neq0\), then
\[
v^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_{3,q}v
=2u^2+(qu-w)^2+2w^2>0.
\]
Thus both \(\Psi_q\) and \(\Gamma_{3,q}\) are positive definite. Direct multiplication yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_q\Sigma_1A_q^{\mathsf T}&=\Psi_q,\\
A_q\Sigma_2A_q^{\mathsf T}&=\Psi_q+\operatorname{diag}(1,0),\\
A_q\Gamma_{3,q}A_q^{\mathsf T}&=\Psi_q+\operatorname{diag}(0,1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(A_q\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma_{3,q})\). Since \(q\neq0\), \(A_q\neq I_2\). The matrices \(\Gamma_{3,q}\) are pairwise distinct because their off-diagonal entry is \(-q\).

Suppose, for contradiction, that a deterministic finite-membership-query procedure computes the exact union for every arbitrary nonempty region family. Run it on the singleton regions
\[
\mathcal C^0_1=\{\Sigma_1\},\qquad
\mathcal C^0_2=\{\Sigma_2\},\qquad
\mathcal C^0_3=\{\Sigma_3\}.
\]
Its required output is \(\{I_2\}\). Only finitely many matrices are queried from the third oracle. Since the family \((\Gamma_{3,q}:q\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0\})\) is infinite and pairwise distinct, choose \(q\neq0\) for which \(\Gamma_{3,q}\) was not queried. Replace only the third region by
\[
\mathcal C^1_3=\{\Sigma_3,\Gamma_{3,q}\}.
\]
Induction over the query number shows that the two runs have identical transcripts. Initially their internal states agree. If their transcripts agree before a query, determinism selects the same region and matrix. Answers from the first two oracles agree because those regions are unchanged. Answers from the third agree along the original transcript because membership differs only at the unqueried point \(\Gamma_{3,q}\). Hence the next internal states also agree. The original run terminates after finitely many queries, so the modified run terminates with the same output \(\{I_2\}\).

But the modified exact union contains \(A_q\), because
\[
A_q\in\mathcal R_0(\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma_{3,q}),
\]
whereas \(A_q\notin\{I_2\}\). This contradiction proves the finite-membership-query obstruction. The witness consists entirely of rational positive-definite matrices and has \(\gamma_H=1\), so the obstruction is about input representation rather than vanishing affine separation."}

Because \(\gamma_H\geq\gamma_0>0\), \(\text{def:affine-separation}\) implies \(q\geq3\).

\textbf{Uniform matrix bounds.} Let \(G\) be either structural matrix \(D\) or an audited candidate matrix \(A\). In the Leibniz expansion of \(\det G\), the identity permutation contributes one because \(G\) has unit diagonal. Every nonidentity permutation decomposes into disjoint directed cycles and fixed points. The absolute value of each nontrivial cycle product is at most \(1-\zeta_0<1\), and every fixed-point factor is one. Thus every one of the \(p!\) Leibniz terms has absolute value at most one, whence
\[
|\det G|\leq p!.
\tag{1}
\]
If \(\sigma_1(G)=\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), the condition-number bound makes every other singular value at least \(\sigma_1(G)/\overline\kappa\). Therefore
\[
\frac{\sigma_1(G)^p}{\overline\kappa^{p-1}}
\leq\prod_{j=1}^p\sigma_j(G)=|\det G|\leq p!,
\]
so
\[
\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq L_0.
\tag{2}
\]
Since \(G_{ii}=1\), \(\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\geq1\), and hence
\[
\|G^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq\overline\kappa/\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq\overline\kappa.
\tag{3}
\]

\textbf{Compactness and the global residual gap.} Every defining condition of \(\mathfrak T\) is closed. Inverses are encoded by \(DU=UD=I_p\) and \(AV=VA=I_p\); cycle slack is a finite family of weak polynomial inequalities; affine separation is a finite conjunction of disjunctions of weak polynomial inequalities; and the PSD conditions \(\Omega,\Psi\succeq0\) and covariance-interiority conditions \(\Sigma_e,\Gamma_e\succeq\lambda_0I_p\) are closed. Equations (2)--(3) bound \(D,A,U,V\). Each scale inequality bounds the PSD nuisance, all covariance matrices, and every nonnegative shift coordinate on its side. Thus every fixed \((H_1,H_2,S)\)-piece is closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and is compact by \(\text{lem:compact-continuous-minimum}\). Their finite union \(\mathfrak T\) is compact, and its closed far subfamily \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) is compact.

If \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\neq\varnothing\), continuity of \(\mathfrak r\) and \(\text{lem:compact-continuous-minimum}\) give a minimizer. Suppose its residual were zero. Then on \(S\),
\[
D\Sigma_eD^{\mathsf T}=\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e),
\qquad
A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e),
\qquad e\in S.
\tag{4}
\]
For each \(k<\ell\), the first design's affine-separation constraint supplies a triple in \(S\) with affine minor of absolute value at least \(\gamma_0\); hence its \((k,\ell)\)-cloud on \(S\) is not contained in an affine line.

There are \(|E\setminus S|=m-q=2c\) remaining labels. Partition them into disjoint sets \(C_1,C_2\) of cardinality \(c\). Extend the first explanation to \(S\cup C_1\) by using zero shifts and covariance \(D^{-1}\Omega D^{-\mathsf T}\) on \(C_1\), and extend the second to \(S\cup C_2\) by using zero shifts and covariance \(A^{-1}\Psi A^{-\mathsf T}\) on \(C_2\). The nuisance matrices are only required to be PSD, so these auxiliary covariances are PSD; no positive-definiteness claim is needed. Both added shift vectors are nonnegative. The two fitted sets have size \(q+c=h\), intersect exactly in \(S\), and (4) makes the explanations agree there. The hypotheses of \(\text{lem:overlap-uniqueness}\), which accepts PSD invariant nuisances and covariance slots, now hold. It follows that \(A=D\). Since \(U=D^{-1}\), this gives \(AU=I_p\), contrary to \(\|AU-I_p\|_{\mathrm F}\geq\rho_0>0\). Therefore
\[
\mu_0>0.
\tag{5}
\]
The same conclusion holds by definition when the far family is empty.

All coefficients describing \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) are rational or effectively specified real algebraic numbers, and the latter have rational polynomial equations with isolating sign conditions. For rational \(d>0\), the assertion that some \(\tau\in\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\) satisfies \(\mathfrak r(\tau)<d\) is first-order rational-polynomial after squaring the Frobenius-norm inequalities. It is decidable by \(\text{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\). By (5), the assertion is false for all sufficiently small dyadic \(d=2^{-j}\). Hence the search terminates and returns
\[
0<\underline\mu\leq\mu_0,
\qquad
r_0=\frac{\underline\mu}{2\sqrt p\,L_0^2}>0.
\tag{6}
\]

\textbf{Entry into the identity chart.} Fix \(A\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). Exactness of the released code from \(\text{thm:certified-inference-representation-obstruction}\) supplies \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\), matrices \(\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\), a nuisance \(\Psi\succeq0\), and nonnegative shifts \(t_e\) such that
\[
A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e),
\qquad e\in K.
\tag{7}
\]

\[
\|\Gamma_e-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq r_{n,\alpha,H},
\qquad e\in S.
\tag{8}
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
\left\|A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}-\Psi-\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\right\|_{\mathrm F}
&=\left\|A(\Sigma_e-\Gamma_e)A^{\mathsf T}\right\|_{\mathrm F}\\
&\leq\sqrt p\,L_0^2r_{n,\alpha,H}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]

\[
Q=AD^{-1}=I_p+R,
\qquad u=\|R\|_{\mathrm F},
\]
one has
\[
u<\rho_0\leq1,
\qquad K_0\overline M u\leq\frac12.
\tag{10}
\]

For each \(i<j\), affine separation supplies a triple in \(S\) with determinant of absolute value at least \(\gamma_0\). Expanding that determinant into the three pairwise cross-products based at \(e_0\) and applying the triangle inequality supplies \(e,f\in S\) such that
\[
|x_{ei}x_{fj}-x_{ej}x_{fi}|\geq\gamma_0/3.
\tag{11}
\]

\[
Q\operatorname{diag}(x_e)Q^{\mathsf T}
+A(E_e-E_{e_0})A^{\mathsf T}
\]
therefore gives
\[
R_{ij}x_{ej}+R_{ji}x_{ei}
=-\sum_{k=1}^pR_{ik}R_{jk}x_{ek}
-[A(E_e-E_{e_0})A^{\mathsf T}]_{ij}.

\leq(1+u)L_0.

\[

\leq\overline M u^2
+2r_{n,\alpha,H}L_0^2(1+u)^2.
\tag{13}
\]

\[
|R_{ij}|\leq\frac{6\overline M}{\gamma_0}
\left\{\overline M u^2
+2r_{n,\alpha,H}L_0^2(1+u)^2\right\}.
\tag{14}
\]
The unit diagonals of \(A\) and \(D\) give
\[
0=(A-D)_{ii}=(RD)_{ii}
=R_{ii}+\sum_{k\neq i}R_{ik}D_{ki}.
\tag{15}
\]
For each \(i\), the squared norm of the \(i\)-th column of \(D\) is at most \(L_0^2\). Summing the squared off-diagonal bounds in (14), applying Cauchy--Schwarz to (15), and taking square roots yields
\[
u\leq K_0\left\{\overline M u^2
+2r_{n,\alpha,H}L_0^2(1+u)^2\right\}.
\tag{16}
\]
By (10), the first term on the right of (16) is at most \(u/2\), and \((1+u)^2\leq4\). Hence
\[
u\leq16K_0L_0^2r_{n,\alpha,H}.
\tag{17}
\]

\[
\|A-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=\|RD\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq uL_0
\leq16K_0L_0^3r_{n,\alpha,H}
=C_0r_{n,\alpha,H}.
\tag{18}
\]
Taking the supremum over \(A\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) proves the outer-radius bound. On the coverage event, \(D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) by \(\text{thm:certified-inference-representation-obstruction}\), so the union is nonempty. For \(A_1,A_2\) in it, the triangle inequality and (18) give \(\|A_1-A_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2C_0r_{n,\alpha,H}\), proving the diameter bound. The constants use only the fixed dimensions and five audit thresholds, which proves uniformity and the stated limits."}

No contraction is asserted on an abstaining outcome, beyond the radius \(r_0\), or for an unrestricted confidence union that fails the universal audit, and no numerical or CRAN implementation is asserted.","free_symbols":["CertificateInferenceHandle","Ualpha","Calpha","Sigma","D","Omega","H","PSDp","Rc","rRadius","outerOp","diamOp","AuditedReleaseContraction","p","m","c","h","n","alpha","gamma0","zeta0","lambda0","kappabar","Mbar"],"depends_on":["ass:backshift-normalization","ass:nonnegative-shifts","ass:honest-covariance-model","def:admissible-matrices","def:compatible-set","def:encoded-covariance-regions","def:honest-region-radius","def:operator-diameter","def:operator-outer-radius","def:confidence-union","def:certificate-inference-handle","def:audited-release-contraction","thm:confidence-union-coverage","thm:non-effective-margin-contraction"],"status":"proved","justification":"This is the certified symbolic result: exact population classification and universal covariance-interiority auditing, model-conditional coverage under PSD invariant noise, boundary abstention, and uniform linear contraction on covered outcomes released after the audit.","gap":"The theorem deliberately leaves contraction on audit-failure outcomes, contraction beyond the certified radius, and practical numerical or CRAN software unresolved; it does not claim that the universal audit must pass.","consumer":"The theorem and subset-consensus definition specify a future corruption-aware pooled-difference workflow: enumerate size-\(h\) subsets, enforce normalized congruence feasibility with a common PSD nuisance and nonnegative raw shifts, return the full candidate union, and abstain when the universal audit fails.","proof_tex":"Fix the integers, probability level, and rational thresholds in the statement. \quad

\[

\qquad

\qquad
\kappa(w_0)=\kappa_D,

\leq C_0r_{n,\alpha,H},

\leq2C_0r_{n,\alpha,H}.

That theorem gives the displayed values of \(L_0,K_0,C_0\) and shows that they depend only on the fixed dimensions and audit thresholds. Along a covered, released sequence with \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\to0\), the fixed positive radius condition holds eventually and both bounds converge to zero. Every conclusion was conditioned on coverage, release, and the certified radius, so none is asserted on abstaining outcomes or beyond \(r_0\), and the argument constructs a symbolic specification rather than numerical or CRAN software."}

Both \(D\) and \(A\) have unit diagonal; for every directed simple cycle \(C\), the corresponding products in \(I_p-D\) and \(I_p-A\) have absolute value at most \(1-\zeta _0\); and
\[

\]

{"id":"thm:non-effective-margin-contraction","kind":"theorem","statement":"Fix \(p\geq2\), \(m\geq1\), and \(0\leq c\leq m-1\), put \(h=m-c\) and \(q=m-2c=h-c\), and fix \(\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) and \(\overline\kappa,\overline M\in\mathbb Q\cap[1,\infty)\). Define
\[
L_0=\bigl(p!\,\overline\kappa^{p-1}\bigr)^{1/p},
\qquad
K_0=\frac{6\overline M}{\gamma_0}
\sqrt{p(p-1)(1+L_0^2)},
\qquad
C_0=16K_0L_0^3.
\]
Under \(\text{ass:backshift-normalization}\), \(\text{ass:nonnegative-shifts}\), and \(\text{ass:honest-covariance-model}\), suppose that \(\Omega\in\mathbb S_+^p\) and that the true instance satisfies
\[
\gamma_H\geq\gamma_0,\qquad
\zeta_D\geq\zeta_0,\qquad
\lambda_{\mathrm{cov},H}\geq\lambda_0,\qquad
\kappa_D\leq\overline\kappa,\qquad
M_H\leq\overline M.
\]
Fix \(n\geq1\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and an arbitrary indexed family of nonempty covariance regions \(\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\subseteq\mathbb S_{++}^p\). For a set \(K\subseteq E\) of size \(h\) and shifts \((t_e:e\in K)\), define \(\gamma_K(t)=0\) when \(q<3\), and otherwise define
\[
\gamma_K(t)=
\min_{1\leq k<\ell\leq p}
\min_{\substack{S\subseteq K\\|S|=q}}
\max_{e<f<g\in S}
\left|
\det\begin{pmatrix}
1&t_{ek}&t_{e\ell}\\
1&t_{fk}&t_{f\ell}\\
1&t_{gk}&t_{g\ell}
\end{pmatrix}
\right|.
\]
Assume declaratively that every tuple consisting of \(K\subseteq E\) with \(|K|=h\), \(A\in\mathcal D\), \(\Psi\in\mathbb S_+^p\), \(t_e\in[0,\infty)^p\), and \(\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) for \(e\in K\), satisfying
\[
A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)
\qquad(e\in K),
\]
also satisfies all five bounds
\[
\gamma_K(t)\geq\gamma_0,qquad
1-\operatorname{CP}(I_p-A)\geq\zeta_0,qquad
\min_{e\in K}\lambda_{\min}(\Gamma_e)\geq\lambda_0,
\]
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq\overline\kappa,qquad
1+\|\Psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\max_{e\in K}\|\Gamma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\max_{e\in K}\|\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq\overline M.
\]
Then there exists a real number \(r_0>0\), depending only on \(p,m,c,\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\lambda_0,\overline\kappa,\overline M\), such that on the event
\[
G_{n,\alpha,H}
=\{\Sigma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\text{ for every }e\in H\},
\]
one has
\[
r_{n,\alpha,H}\leq r_0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha,D)
\leq C_0r_{n,\alpha,H},
\]
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha)
\leq2C_0r_{n,\alpha,H}.
\]
Consequently, along any sequence of covered outcomes satisfying the same declarative candidate-side bounds and \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\to0\), both displayed set radii converge to zero. The existence of \(r_0\) is non-effective: no procedure is asserted for checking the universal candidate premise or for computing \(r_0\).","free_symbols":["p","m","c","h","E","gamma0","zeta0","lambda0","kappabar","Mbar","gamma","zeta","lambda","kappa","Mbound","D","Omega","s","Sigma","H","Calpha","Ualpha","Rc","Dcal","CP","PSDp","SPDp","n","alpha","rRadius","outerOp","diamOp"],"depends_on":["ass:backshift-normalization","ass:nonnegative-shifts","ass:honest-covariance-model","def:admissible-matrices","def:affine-separation","def:compatible-set","def:honest-region-radius","def:operator-diameter","def:operator-outer-radius","def:confidence-union","lem:overlap-uniqueness","thm:confidence-union-coverage"],"status":"proved","justification":"Declarative five-margin bounds make the universal two-explanation family compact; overlap uniqueness creates a positive far-family residual gap, and affine-minor inversion then gives the explicit local linear modulus.","gap":"The radius is an existential compactness minimum. The theorem supplies neither a test of the candidate-wide premise nor an effective way to evaluate the radius.","consumer":"The result gives an optional analytic contraction guarantee for arbitrary covariance-region unions when all feasible size-\(h\) explanations are known declaratively to remain in one fixed compact, separated class.","proof_tex":"Put \(q=m-2c=h-c\). By \(\text{def:affine-separation}\), \(q<3\) would imply \(\gamma_H=0\), contradicting \(\gamma_H\geq\gamma_0>0\). Hence
\[
q\geq3.
\tag{1}
\]

\textbf{Uniform matrix bounds.}
Let \(G\) denote either a true structural matrix or a feasible candidate matrix satisfying the theorem's cycle-slack and condition-number bounds. In the Leibniz expansion of \(\det G\), the identity-permutation term equals one because \(G\) has unit diagonal. Every other permutation decomposes into fixed points and disjoint directed simple cycles. Every nontrivial cycle product in \(I_p-G\) has absolute value at most \(1-\zeta_0<1\), while every fixed-point factor has absolute value one. Thus each of the \(p!\) Leibniz terms has absolute value at most one, and
\[
|\det G|\leq p!.
\tag{2}
\]
Write \(\sigma_1(G)=\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) and order the singular values decreasingly. The condition-number bound implies \(\sigma_j(G)\geq\sigma_1(G)/\overline\kappa\) for \(2\leq j\leq p\). Therefore
\[
\frac{\sigma_1(G)^p}{\overline\kappa^{p-1}}
\leq\prod_{j=1}^p\sigma_j(G)
=|\det G|
\leq p!,
\]
and hence
\[
\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq L_0.
\tag{3}
\]
Since a unit diagonal entry gives \(\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\geq1\),
\[
\|G^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=\frac{\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|G^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}}
{\|G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}
\leq\overline\kappa.
\tag{4}
\]

\textbf{A uniform compact residual gap.}
Set
\[
\rho_0=min\left\{1,\frac{1}{2K_0\overline M}\right\}>0.
\tag{5}
\]
For each choice of sets \(H_1,H_2\subseteq E\) of size \(h\) and \(S\subseteq H_1\cap H_2\) of size \(q\), consider tuples
\[
\tau=\bigl(H_1,H_2,S,D,U,\Omega,(s_e,\Sigma_e)_{e\in H_1},
A,V,\Psi,(t_e,\Gamma_e)_{e\in H_2}\bigr)
\]
subject to the following closed conditions: \(DU=UD=I_p\) and \(AV=VA=I_p\); both structural matrices have unit diagonal, cycle slack at least \(\zeta_0\), and condition number at most \(\overline\kappa\); \(\Omega,\Psi\succeq0\), \(\Sigma_e,\Gamma_e\succeq\lambda_0I_p\), and \(s_e,t_e\in[0,\infty)^p\); each side satisfies its BACKSHIFT covariance equations; each side's affine separation, computed over every \(q\)-element subset of its size-\(h\) fitted set, is at least \(\gamma_0\); and each side satisfies the displayed scale bound with upper bound \(\overline M\). Let \(\mathfrak T\) be the finite union of these tuple families.

The inverse equations and (3)--(4) bound \(D,U,A,V\). The scale bounds separately bound the positive-semidefinite nuisances, all covariance matrices, and every nonnegative shift coordinate. Every remaining constraint is closed: the cycle conditions and affine-minor conditions are finite weak polynomial inequalities, the cone constraints are closed, and the covariance and inverse relations are polynomial equalities. Thus every fixed-index piece is closed and bounded in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. By the finite-dimensional Heine--Borel theorem it is compact, and therefore the finite union \(\mathfrak T\) is compact.

Define the continuous residual
\[
\mathfrak r(\tau)=
\max_{e\in S}
\left\|A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}
-\Psi-\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\right\|_{\mathrm F}
\]
and the closed far family
\[
\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}
=\{\tau\in\mathfrak T:\|AU-I_p\|_{\mathrm F}\geq\rho_0\}.
\]
If \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}=\varnothing\), set \(\mu_0=1\). Otherwise compactness and continuity give an attained minimum
\[
\mu_0=\min_{\tau\in\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}}\mathfrak r(\tau).
\tag{6}
\]
We show that this minimum is positive. If a far tuple had \(\mathfrak r(\tau)=0\), then on \(S\)
\[
D\Sigma_eD^{\mathsf T}=\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e),
\qquad
A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e).
\tag{7}
\]
For each \(k<\ell\), the first side's affine-separation condition supplies three labels in \(S\) whose affine minor has absolute value at least \(\gamma_0\). Hence the first side's \((k,\ell)\)-shift cloud on \(S\) is not contained in an affine line.

Because \(|E\setminus S|=m-q=2c\), partition \(E\setminus S\) into disjoint sets \(C_1,C_2\) of cardinality \(c\). Extend the first explanation to \(S\cup C_1\) by assigning zero shifts and covariance \(D^{-1}\Omega D^{-\mathsf T}\) on \(C_1\), and extend the second explanation to \(S\cup C_2\) by assigning zero shifts and covariance \(A^{-1}\Psi A^{-\mathsf T}\) on \(C_2\). These added covariances are positive semidefinite because the nuisances are positive semidefinite and the structural matrices are invertible; the added shifts are nonnegative. The two fitted sets have cardinality \(q+c=h\), their intersection is \(S\), and (7) makes their covariance equations agree on that intersection. All hypotheses of \(\text{lem:overlap-uniqueness}\) therefore hold, so \(A=D\). Since \(U=D^{-1}\), this gives \(AU=I_p\), contradicting membership in \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\). Thus
\[
\mu_0>0.
\tag{8}
\]
This also holds under the convention \(\mu_0=1\) when the far family is empty. Define, non-effectively,
\[
r_0=\frac{\mu_0}{2\sqrt p\,L_0^2}>0.
\tag{9}
\]
Because \(\mathfrak T\), and hence \(\mu_0\), was defined solely from the fixed dimensions and the five numerical bounds, \(r_0\) has exactly the asserted uniform dependence. No decision or computation of \(\mu_0\) is used.

\textbf{Entry into the identity neighborhood.}
Fix an outcome in \(G_{n,\alpha,H}\), let \(r=r_{n,\alpha,H}\leq r_0\), and take any \(A\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\). By \(\text{def:confidence-union}\), select \(\Gamma_e\in\mathcal C^{(n)}_{e,\alpha}\) for all \(e\in E\) such that \(A\in\mathcal R_c(\Gamma)\). By \(\text{def:compatible-set}\), there are a fitted set of size at least \(h\), a nuisance \(\Psi\succeq0\), and nonnegative shifts satisfying the candidate covariance equations. Restrict the fitted set and its witnesses to a subset \(K\subseteq E\) of size exactly \(h\). The theorem's declarative candidate hypothesis supplies all five candidate-side bounds on this restriction.

Inclusion--exclusion gives
\[
|H\cap K|\geq|H|+|K|-|E|=2h-m=q.
\]
Choose \(S\subseteq H\cap K\) with \(|S|=q\). Put \(U=D^{-1}\) and \(V=A^{-1}\). The true and candidate equations and their respective five bounds show that the resulting objects form a tuple in \(\mathfrak T\). Since the outcome is covered and \(e\in S\subseteq H\),
\[
\|\Gamma_e-\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq r
\qquad(e\in S).
\tag{10}
\]
The candidate covariance equation, (3), (10), submultiplicativity, and \(\|X\|_{\mathrm F}\leq\sqrt p\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left\|A\Sigma_eA^{\mathsf T}
-\Psi-\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\right\|_{\mathrm F}
&=\left\|A(\Sigma_e-\Gamma_e)A^{\mathsf T}\right\|_{\mathrm F}\\
&\leq\sqrt p\,L_0^2r
\leq\mu_0/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
If the tuple belonged to \(\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{far}}\), then in the nonempty-far case (6) would make the maximum in (11) at least \(\mu_0\), a contradiction; in the empty-far case membership is impossible by definition. Consequently, with
\[
Q=AD^{-1}=I_p+R,
\qquad u=\|R\|_{\mathrm F},
\]
one has
\[
u<\rho_0\leq1,
\qquad K_0\overline M u\leq\frac12.
\tag{12}
\]

\textbf{Local affine-minor inversion.}
Fix \(e_0\in S\) and write \(x_e=s_e-s_{e_0}\). For every \(i<j\), the true-side affine-separation bound supplies a triple \(a,b,d\in S\) whose \((i,j)\) affine determinant has absolute value at least \(\gamma_0\). Writing \(\widetilde x_e=(x_{ei},x_{ej})\in\mathbb R^2\), translation invariance of the affine determinant and the identity
\[
\det(\widetilde x_a-\widetilde x_b,
\widetilde x_d-\widetilde x_b)
=\det(\widetilde x_a,\widetilde x_d)
+\det(\widetilde x_d,\widetilde x_b)
+\det(\widetilde x_b,\widetilde x_a)
\]
show, by the triangle inequality, that two labels \(e,f\in S\) satisfy
\[
|x_{ei}x_{fj}-x_{ej}x_{fi}|\geq\gamma_0/3.
\tag{13}
\]
Let \(E_e=\Gamma_e-\Sigma_e\). Subtract the candidate equation at \(e_0\) from that at \(e\), and subtract the true covariance equation at \(e_0\) from that at \(e\). The common nuisances cancel. Taking the \((i,j)\) off-diagonal entry yields
\[
R_{ij}x_{ej}+R_{ji}x_{ei}
=-\sum_{k=1}^pR_{ik}R_{jk}x_{ek}
-[A(E_e-E_{e_0})A^{\mathsf T}]_{ij}.
\tag{14}
\]
The scale and nonnegativity conditions give \(|x_{ek}|\leq\overline M\). Equation (10) gives \(\|E_e-E_{e_0}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2r\), and
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|QD\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq(1+u)L_0.
\]
Consequently, Cauchy--Schwarz and \(\sum_k|R_{ik}R_{jk}|\leq u^2\) turn (14) into
\[
|R_{ij}x_{ej}+R_{ji}x_{ei}|
\leq\overline M u^2+2rL_0^2(1+u)^2.
\tag{15}
\]
Apply (15) at the two labels from (13) and solve the resulting two-by-two linear system for \(R_{ij}\) and \(R_{ji}\). Each coefficient has absolute value at most \(\overline M\), so Cramer's rule and (13) give, for every ordered pair \(i\neq j\),
\[
|R_{ij}|
\leq\frac{6\overline M}{\gamma_0}
\left\{\overline M u^2+2rL_0^2(1+u)^2\right\}.
\tag{16}
\]
The unit diagonals of \(A\) and \(D\) imply
\[
0=(A-D)_{ii}=(RD)_{ii}
=R_{ii}+\sum_{k\neq i}R_{ik}D_{ki}.
\tag{17}
\]
For each \(i\), the squared norm of the \(i\)-th column of \(D\) is at most \(L_0^2\). Squaring (16), summing over the \(p(p-1)\) ordered off-diagonal entries, applying Cauchy--Schwarz to (17), and taking square roots therefore yield
\[
u\leq K_0
\left\{\overline M u^2+2rL_0^2(1+u)^2\right\}.
\tag{18}
\]
By (12), the quadratic term on the right is at most \(u/2\), and \((1+u)^2\leq4\). Hence
\[
u\leq16K_0L_0^2r.
\tag{19}
\]
It follows that
\[
\|A-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=\|RD\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq uL_0
\leq16K_0L_0^3r
=C_0r.
\tag{20}
\]
Taking the supremum over \(A\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\) proves the outer-radius bound. The coverage theorem gives \(D\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\), so the union is nonempty. For \(A_1,A_2\in\mathcal U^{(n)}_\alpha\), the triangle inequality and (20) give
\[
\|A_1-A_2\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq\|A_1-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|A_2-D\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq2C_0r,
\]
which proves the diameter bound. Because the same \(r_0\) and \(C_0\) apply throughout the fixed-margin class, \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\to0\) on covered outcomes implies both asserted limits."}

directive:
INFERENCE-SCOPE MAXIMIZATION ONLY. Preserve byte-for-byte the five frozen population nodes lem:overlap-uniqueness, thm:sharp-replacement-radius, prop:generic-support-frontier, lem:generic-affine-occupancy, and prop:uniform-support-deletion-radius, including every statement, proof, dependency, status, and note. Keep thm:sharp-replacement-radius as the sole headline. Do not alter delta_H>c, gamma_H>0, the m-2c overlap elbow, the SPD legal converse, the PSD-class minimax transfer, the four-term occupancy formula, T<m-2c, or the exact deletion budget.

Rework only the inference carrier and thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction.

1. Broaden Calpha, def:confidence-union, thm:confidence-union-coverage, thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction, and the OEQ input carrier from arbitrary nonempty subsets of SPDp to arbitrary nonempty subsets of PSDp. Reprove the changed inference nodes; neither proof uses covariance invertibility.

2. Keep the theorem's four TRUE-side bounds gamma_H>=gamma0, zeta_D>=zeta0, kappa_D<=kappabar, and M_H<=Mbar. In its universal FEASIBLE-CANDIDATE premise retain only normalization slack 1-CP(I-A)>=zeta0 and structural condition number ||A||op ||A^-1||op<=kappabar. Delete candidate-side gamma_K(t)>=gamma0 and the global candidate scale inequality. Candidate affine separation is never used: exact far-family exclusion and local affine-minor inversion use only the true shifts on S subset H intersect K. Candidate global scale is derivable locally and need not be assumed.

3. Let L0 remain as stated. Restrict the comparison family's candidate nuisance/shift variables to the overlap S. For entry radii r<=1, true M_H<=Mbar gives ||Sigma_e||op<=Mbar-1 and hence ||Gamma_e||op<=Mbar on e in S. Since Psi and diag(t_e) are PSD summands of A Gamma_e A^T and ||A||op<=L0, derive ||Psi||op<=L0^2 Mbar and ||diag(t_e)||op<=L0^2 Mbar. Use these derived bounds in the compact far-family; impose no candidate gamma bound. A zero residual still supplies two exact explanations on S, and TRUE-side gamma_H>=gamma0 lets lem:overlap-uniqueness force A=D. Define r0=min{1, mu0/(2 sqrt(p) L0^2)}. Retain the existing local inversion and displayed C0 bound. Keep r0 existential/non-effective and claim no procedure for checking the remaining candidate premise or computing r0.

4. Preserve oeq:certified-uniform-inference as the sole open node and preserve every executable QE, exact-code, rational classification, effective-radius, chart, and software task as unresolved. It may retain a conservative future universal four-margin audit as a way to certify unknown true-side margins, but distinguish that operational sufficient audit from the analytically minimal contraction theorem: the proved contraction itself needs true-side four margins and only candidate-side normalization slack plus conditioning. Do not claim that a zero-affine-separation alternative obstructs contraction around a fixed true instance already satisfying gamma_H>=gamma0.

5. SYNC THE PROSE FIELDS tldr, project_justification.gap/niche/fill, related_work, interpretation, honest_scope, technical_internal_limitation, sampling_model, relevant theorem/OEQ notes, comparator table, and open_obligations. State PSD-region coverage, true-side four margins, only two candidate-side analytic bounds, non-effective r0, and exclusively open executable/effective work. Treat the three current PROSE-OPEN-OVERCLAIM warnings as false positives, not defects to cure by weakening proved claims.

Can one additionally build and formally verify an executable real-closed-field quantifier-elimination, sign-determination, and root-isolation substrate which, from finite rational-semialgebraic covariance-region codes, (i) terminates and emits a quantifier-free code whose realization is exactly \\(\\mathcal U^{(n)}_\\alpha\\), (ii) decides a release-or-abstain condition, possibly using a conservative universal four-margin audit to certify unknown true-side margins and forcing abstention within that audit whenever it finds a feasible candidate with zero affine separation, while distinguishing that operational sufficient audit from the sole candidate-side condition-number bound required by the analytic contraction theorem, (iii) decides for every rational population covariance family whether \\(\\mathcal R_c(\\Sigma)\\) is empty, is a singleton, or contains at least two matrices, and (iv) computes a certified positive lower bound for the compact far-family residual and hence an effective positive radius \\(r_0\\)? Can the same verified program automate normalization-chart changes without altering the represented matrix set and support a corruption-aware extension of the CRAN \\(\\texttt{backShift}\\) workflow? Every executable, effective, decision, chart-automation, and software item in this question is unresolved future work. A feasible candidate with zero affine separation or a small normalization slack may trigger that conservative operational audit, but neither is an analytic candidate-side obstruction to contraction around a fixed true instance satisfying \\(\\gamma_H\\geq\\gamma_0>0\\) and \\(\\zeta_D\\geq\\zeta_0>0\\).","free_symbols":["Sigma","Calpha","Ualpha","Rc","rRadius","diamOp","outerOp","gamma","kappa","zeta","Mbound","gamma0","zeta0","kappabar","Mbar","D","p","m","c","H","E","n","alpha"],"depends_on":["ass:backshift-normalization","ass:nonnegative-shifts","ass:honest-covariance-model","def:admissible-matrices","def:compatible-set","def:affine-separation","def:subset-consensus","def:honest-region-radius","def:operator-diameter","def:operator-outer-radius","def:confidence-union","thm:confidence-union-coverage","thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction"],"status":"to-prove","justification":"Positive-semidefinite set-theoretic coverage and non-effective contraction under four true-side margins and only candidate conditioning are established. The remaining question is a formally verified executable algebraic and software interface.","gap":"Every code-generation, exact-decision, effective-radius, normalization-chart automation, release-or-abstain, and CRAN implementation item remains unresolved.
